questions.question: Who was the leader that defeated Krishnadevaraya of Vijayanagara in the Battle of Raichur?
questions.solution:
• The Battle of Raichur (1520) was fought between Krishnadevaraya of Vijayanagara and Ismail Adil Shah of Bijapur over the Raichur Doab.
  • Though Krishnadevaraya initially won, Adil Shah of Bijapur was the ruler who opposed him in this decisive conflict.

questions.question: The founders of Vijayanagar empire, Harihara and Bukka Raya were the ministers of:
questions.solution:
• Harihara and Bukka Raya were ministers of Kampili.
  • The Vijayanagara Empire was established in 1336 by the brothers of the Sangama dynasty.
  • Between 1336 and 1565, Vijayanagara was ruled by the Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, and Aravidu dynasties.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding foreign travellers to Vijayanagar:
Statement 1: Domingo Paes, a Portuguese traveller, visited the Vijayanagar empire during the reign of Krishnadevaraya.
Statement 2: Niccolo de Conti visited the Vijayanagar empire during the reign of Krishnadevaraya.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true
questions.solution:
• Statement 1 is correct: Domingo Paes, a Portuguese traveller, visited Vijayanagar during Krishnadevaraya's reign and described its prosperity and military strength.
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: Niccolo de Conti visited India earlier during the rule of Devaraya I, not Krishnadevaraya.

questions.question: Which of the following was the last dynasty of the Vijayanagara Empire?
questions.solution:
• The Aravidu dynasty was the last dynasty of the Vijayanagara Empire.
  • The four dynasties in order:
    • Sangama dynasty (1336-1485 CE)
    • Saluva dynasty (1485-1505 CE)
    • Tuluva dynasty (1505-1570 CE)
    • Aravidu dynasty (1570-1646 CE)

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Vijayanagara rulers:
1. Achyuta Deva Raya assumed the title of 'Establisher of the Yavana kingdom'.
2. Krishna Deva Raya founded Nagalapuram in memory of his mother.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.solution:
• Statement 1 is incorrect: The title 'Establisher of the Yavana kingdom' was taken by Krishna Deva Raya, not Achyuta Deva Raya.
  • Statement 2 is correct: Krishna Deva Raya founded Nagalapuram in memory of his mother.

questions.question: The Vijayanagara empire included people from different cultural regions. Which of the following regions was NOT a part of it?
questions.solution:
• The Maratha region was NOT a part of the Vijayanagara Empire.
  • The Vijayanagara Empire primarily included Tamil, Karnataka, and Telugu-speaking areas.
  • The Maratha region was ruled by the Yadava Dynasty and later the Bahmani Sultanate during Vijayanagara's peak.

questions.question: What was the dominant source of income in the Vijayanagar Empire?
questions.solution:
• Land revenue was the dominant source of income in the Vijayanagar Empire.
  • Other sources included tributes, gifts from vassals and feudal chiefs, and customs at ports.

questions.question: Who among the following Vijayanagar rulers married his daughter to Firuz Shah Bahmani?
questions.solution:
• Deva Raya I married his daughter to Firuz Shah Bahmani.
  • In 1406-07, Firuz Shah of the Bahmani Sultanate defeated Deva Raya I of the Vijayanagara Empire.

questions.question: The founders of Vijayanagara Empire were the feudatories of which of the following dynasties?
questions.solution: • The founders of the Vijayanagara Empire were feudatories of the Kakatiya dynasty.

questions.question: The origin of 'Carnatic music' is related to which of the following Dynasties?
questions.solution:
• The origin of Carnatic music is related to the Vijayanagar Dynasty.
  • Purandara Dasa, a poet-composer of Vijayanagar, is known as the 'Father of Carnatic Music'.

questions.question: Vijayanagara emperor Krishnadeva Raya founded a suburban township near Vijayanagara called Nagalapuram after his
questions.solution: • Krishnadeva Raya founded Nagalapuram in memory of his mother.

questions.question: The local communities of merchants were known as ______ in the Vijayanagara empire.
questions.solution:
• Kudirai Chettis (Horse merchants) were the local communities of merchants in the Vijayanagara empire.
  • Rachavarus (Rajulu) were associated with the ruling dynasty.
  • Narapati (Rayas) meant 'Lord of Men'.
  • Gajapati meant 'Lord of Elephants'.

questions.question:
Match the following terms with their correct description:
A. Pattanulkars → 1. Cavalrymen
B. Bargir → 2. Commercial agent
C. Gomashta → 3. Silk weavers from Gujarat migrated to Vijayanagar
D. Shigdar → 4. Head of Administrative unit (Shiqq)
questions.solution:
• The correct matching is:
    • Pattanulkars - Silk weavers from Gujarat
    • Bargir - Cavalrymen
    • Gomashta - Commercial agent
    • Shigdar - Head of Administrative unit (Shiqq)

questions.question: The Amara-Nayakas were ______ in the Vijayanagara Empire.
questions.solution:
• The Amara-Nayakas were military commanders in the Vijayanagara Empire.
  • They were given territories to govern by the Raya and collected taxes and other dues from peasants, traders, and craftspersons.

questions.question: While historians use the term Vijayanagara Empire, contemporaries of this empire described it as the
questions.solution:
• Contemporaries described the Vijayanagara Empire as 'Karnataka Samaraiyam'.
  • The Vijayanagara Empire (1336-1646) was established by Harihara and Bukka on the banks of the river Tungabhadra.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Raichur Doab:
Statement 1: Raichur Doab refers to the fertile land lying between the rivers Krishna and Tungabhadra.
Statement 2: The Vijayanagar rulers mainly fought the Bengal kingdom for control over Raichur Doab.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is correct, Statement 2 is incorrect
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is incorrect, Statement 2 is correct
questions.solution:
• Statement 1 is correct: Raichur Doab lies between the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers.
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: The Vijayanagar Empire fought the Bahmani Sultanate, not Bengal, for control over Raichur Doab.

questions.question: Which battle led to the destruction of the Vijayanagara empire?
questions.solution:
• The Battle of Talikota (Rakshasi-Tangadi) in 1565 led to the destruction of the Vijayanagara Empire.
  • It was fought between the Vijayanagara Empire and an alliance of the Deccan sultanates.
  • Aliya Rama Raya was defeated and killed, leading to the political collapse of the empire.

questions.question: Provida style of architecture belongs to which empire?
questions.solution:
• Provida style of architecture belongs to the Vijayanagar Empire.
  • Architectural wonders of Vijayanagara: Queen's Bath, Lotus Mahal, Elephant stables, Royal platform, Water tanks.

questions.question: The Anantraj Sagar Tank was built by the ______ rulers.
questions.solution:
• The Anantraj Sagar water storage tank was built by the Vijayanagara rulers.
  • It used a 1.37 km long dam on the Maldevi river, which runs through Nellore district in Andhra Pradesh and empties into the Pennar river.

questions.question: Which Peshwa signed the treaty of Bassein with the East India Company?
questions.solution:
• Baji Rao II signed the Treaty of Bassein (1802) with Lord Wellesley.
  • The Treaty of Surat (1775) was signed between Raghunath Rao and the British.
  • The Treaty of Salbai (1782) was signed between the Maratha Empire and the British East India Company.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Tripartite Treaty of 1838:
Statement 1: The Tripartite Treaty was signed by Shah Shujah, Maharaja Ranjit Singh, and the English East India Company.
Statement 2: The Governor-General of India at the time of this treaty was Lord Auckland.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is correct, Statement 2 is incorrect
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is incorrect, Statement 2 is correct
questions.solution:
• Both statements are correct.
  • The Tripartite Treaty of 1838 was concluded between Maharaja Ranjit Singh of Punjab, Shah Shujah of Afghanistan, and the English Company to reinstall Shah Shujah on the Afghan throne.
  • Lord Auckland was the Governor-General of India at that time.

questions.question: In 1850, Kashmir was sold under which of the following treaties to the Dogra dynasty of Jammu?
questions.solution:
• The Treaty of Amritsar (1846) was executed by the British East India Company and Raja Gulab Singh of Jammu after the First Anglo-Sikh War, under which Kashmir was sold to the Dogra dynasty.
  • Treaty of Allahabad: 1765 between Shah Alam II and Lord Clive.
  • Treaty of Sugaudi: 1815 between Nepal and the East India Company.
  • Treaty of Purandar: 1665 between Jai Singh I and Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj.

questions.question: French possessions in India were restored after the Battle of Wandiwash by the Treaty of ______ signed in the year 1763 between Britain and France.
questions.solution:
• French possessions in India were restored by the Treaty of Paris (1763) between Britain and France.
  • The Battle of Wandiwash was fought in Vandavasi, Tamil Nadu between the French and the British in 1760 as part of the Third Carnatic War.
  • The British defeated the French.

questions.question: The seven years of war in the 18th century was fought between Britain and
questions.solution:
• The Seven Years' War (1756-1763) was fought between Britain and France.
  • It was a global conflict known in America as the 'French and Indian War'.
  • It solidified Britain's stance as the most dominant European country in the world.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the invasion of Delhi in 1739:
Statement 1: Nadir Shah, the Iranian ruler, defeated the Mughal emperor Muhammad Shah at the Battle of Karnal and looted immense wealth from Delhi.
Statement 2: Ahmad Shah Abdali, after the Battle of Karnal, carried away the Kohinoor diamond and the Peacock throne to Iran.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is correct, Statement 2 is incorrect
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is incorrect, Statement 2 is correct
questions.solution:
• Statement 1 is correct: Nadir Shah defeated Mughal emperor Muhammad Shah at the Battle of Karnal and looted Delhi.
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: It was Nadir Shah, not Ahmad Shah Abdali, who took the Kohinoor diamond and the Peacock throne to Persia (Iran).
